Reading preferences and access

More space to read.
A clearer place to think.

The Aa button offers a dyslexia-friendly reading layout. It is a preference, not a diagnosis or treatment, and different readers may prefer different settings.

A quieter layout

Cream reading surfaces, a familiar sans-serif, greater spacing and sentence-case support text. Reduced motion is a separate setting.

Read-aloud

Hear a question or worked steps. The app chooses an available en-GB voice where possible; a British voice cannot be guaranteed on every device.

Clear working

Each mathematical step has its own space. Column exchanges and partial products remain visible, with extra explanation available separately.

Controls and rewards

Buttons and fields support keyboard navigation and visible focus. Phones use the device keyboard and desktop play offers a number pad. Construction activities use labelled controls. Reduced motion keeps text and static feedback available. Dyslexia-friendly layout, reduced motion and read-aloud do not reduce XP, credits or promotion eligibility. Mathematical hints are separately recorded as supported work.

Voice lists are provided by the browser and operating system. A chosen voice may be local or use its provider’s speech service. Written questions and solutions remain available when speech is unavailable.
